ImageDescription.value: Rules covering life membership to the library exchangeable at any library station in the United States, Canada, or Great Britain are provided for the library service. A description of exchange fees charged weekly, and a penny a day when overdue, capped at 25 cents, with a requirement to exchange books four times a month. Books are stored in a Tabard Inn cloth case. Instructions for discontinuing service allow books to be turned in for an out-of-service check that can be exchanged for a book later. Purchase of another book allows membership to continue when books are lost. A table is listed at the bottom to log the activity of the books as they are checked out and returned. The home office of The Tabard Inn Library is listed at Chestnut Street in Philadelphia, PA

Credit.value: Book: The Tree of Knowledge, A document by a woman, published in 1908, Inside front cover

date QS:P571,+1911-00-00T00:00:00Z/9

Collection British Library
Accession number
C188a726
Place of creation Edinburgh and London: T. N. Foulis. 1911. Unpaginated. Twenty-five plates/ photogravures.
Notes The dimensions are estimated. Robin de Beaumont’s small square bookplate is on the upper paper wrapper, verso. He has noted: ‘Roy Cross(?) Bramwell 30.4.2004 £60’. This work is number III of “The Cities Series. Twenty four drawings in photogravure by Jessie M. King./”. The title page and list of contents appear to be photogravures. Each photogravure is mounted on the recto of a backing sheet, with the accompanying text/ caption printed on the facing page. There is a cream-coloured dust jacket over white paper wrappers. The lower cover of the dust jacket is lettered: “/ The city of/ the west. T. N. Foulis. Edinburgh and London/”. The City of Glasgow coat of arms is on the centre. The upper cover features a large group of Glasgow buildings in the background, with a river, trees, a bridge in the foreground. The lettering is: “/ Glasgow/ The city of/ the west/ with drawings by Jessie M. King./” The spine has the letters: “The city of the west” stacked vertically. This book acquired with the generous assistance of the British Library Collections Trust. Another copy (probably) of this work is at British Library shelf mark 10026pp7/3
